expectations.description: Explains Rasch as equal-discrimination across items, while 2PL allows discriminations to vary
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly states: 'Every item has the same discrimination parameter (fixed to 1.0 by convention)' for Rasch, and 'Items are allowed to have their own discrimination parameters (the a parameter)' for 2PL.

expectations.description: Frames the Rasch vs. 2PL choice as a substantive measurement-philosophy decision, not just an AIC/BIC comparison
expectations.evidence: Dedicated section titled 'This is a measurement-philosophy decision, not just a model-fit comparison' explicitly addresses this, calling out the mistake of treating it as a purely empirical AIC/BIC comparison.

expectations.description: Mentions specific objectivity or sample-independence as a property of the Rasch model
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly names 'specific objectivity (or sample-independence)' and explains it: 'the comparison between any two persons does not depend on which particular items were used, and the comparison between any two items does not depend on which persons were sampled.'

expectations.description: States that N = 800 is adequate for 2PL (or for either model)
expectations.evidence: Response states: 'N = 800 is adequate for both models' with specific thresholds: Rasch ~200+, 2PL ~500 minimum, and '800 is solid.'

expectations.description: Provides mirt R code example (mirt::mirt with itemtype='Rasch' and/or '2PL')
expectations.evidence: Full R code block using mirt() with both itemtype='Rasch' and itemtype='2PL', including coef(), itemplot(), and plot() calls.

expectations.description: Mentions item information function (IIF) or test information function (TIF)
expectations.evidence: Dedicated section on 'Item and test information functions' explains both IIF and TIF, and code includes itemplot(..., type='info') and plot(model, type='info').

expectations.description: Does not recommend 3PL as a default for a knowledge test without considering whether guessing is substantively relevant
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly cautions: 'Avoid 3PL unless guessing is substantively meaningful' and 'For a 30-item knowledge test used with students who are engaging seriously, the guessing parameter adds complexity without payoff.'
